# Implement block: Editorial Menu Morph (Jetpack Compose)

You are adding the "Editorial Menu Morph" block from Native Cook to the user's Android app. The block already exists as working Kotlin code. Your job is to bring it into this project faithfully, not to write a new one that looks similar.

## The block

A museum's site, "Orsel, Museum of Form", on warm paper: a spaced serif wordmark, a two-line hamburger with a small "Menu" label, a section kicker with a "01 / 05" index, a two-line Iowan Old Style headline (the system serif on Android), a large hero photo with an italic caption and a "Plan a visit" link. Tapping the hamburger crosses its lines and rolls "Menu" to "Close" while a near-black curtain comes down with a soft, bowed leading edge, the page under it sinking, shrinking slightly and darkening, and five large serif words (Exhibitions, Collection, Architecture, Visit, Journal), each with a small italic number and a small count (12, 4,120, 1911, 10–18, Nº 12), rise letter by letter out of clipped baselines over an opening-hours footer. Running a finger down the words dims all but the one under it, which turns italic, steps right and draws a thin rule under itself; a round photo in a thin paper ring floats beside the finger, chasing it with a lag and leaning into its motion, and wipes up to each word's photo (sculptures and spiral staircases) with a band of colour on the wipe's edge, while the menu turns to that word's colour: oxblood, prussian blue, ochre, verdigris, olive. Lifting on a word flies the photo on a spring into the new page's hero, the circle opening into the hero's rectangle as its ring thins away, as the curtain lifts away above the new page; the card becomes the hero and the page's kicker, headline lines and caption write themselves in as the index rolls to the new number.

**Motion.** Opening plays one timeline from 0 to 1 over 1150 ms (closing back over 900 ms), linearly, and every part eases inside its own slice of it, so closing is the same choreography in reverse. The curtain's edge comes down over 0–0.42 on an ease-in-out (0.77, 0, 0.175, 1); its bottom edge is a cubic whose middle leads the sides by 110 pt × sin(π·progress) in the direction it travels (bowing down while it opens, up while it closes, flat at both ends). The page under it sinks 34 pt, scales to 0.96 and takes a 28% black shade on the same curve. The burger morphs over 0–0.36, its lines first sliding 5 pt together (the shorter one lengthening from 17 to 24 pt) and then turning ±45°, as the header ink goes from near-black to paper and the 14 pt "Menu"/"Close" label rolls up by its own height. Word k (52 pt Iowan Old Style roman, one per 80 pt, in a 66 pt clip box) starts at 0.3 + 0.07k; its letter j rises from below the clip, turning upright from 4°, over 0.012j after that to that plus 0.3 on a strong ease-out (0.23, 1, 0.32, 1); its number, count and italic twin fade or rise over 0.4 from the word's start; the footer rises 16 pt and fades in over 0.68–1. While the menu is open the finger is a pointer from touch down: the word under it crossfades to italic (240 ms), steps 14 pt right (320 ms ease-out) and draws a 1 pt rule under itself left to right (380 ms ease-out, out in 200 ms) while the others dim to 28% (220 ms), with a selection haptic per new word. The preview is a circle 168 pt across with a 3 pt paper-coloured ring drawn just inside its edge; it sits 100 pt right of and 64 pt above the finger, kept on screen, and chases it with an exponential lag of 7/s, leaning 0.012° per pt/s of its sideways speed up to 9°; it appears scaling from 86% over 260 ms. A new word's photo wipes up from the bottom over 460 ms (ease-in-out 0.65, 0, 0.35, 1) while settling from 114% zoom, the old photo filling the part not yet wiped and a 5 pt band of the new word's colour on the edge; the menu's colour crossfades to the word's over 420 ms. Lifting on a fully open menu commits with a light haptic: the card flies on a damped spring (stiffness 180, damping ratio 0.9, mass 1, about 0.6 s) from where it is to the hero's frame inside the sinking page, its size, turn and corners following the spring (the corner radius is half the shorter side × (1 − progress)^1.4, so the circle opens smoothly into the square-cornered hero) while the ring thins from 3 pt and fades out by 60% of the way and the photo drawn "cover" into the moving rect, while the menu closes over 900 ms with the chosen word still lit; once the card has landed and the curtain is gone it hands off to the hero (the same image, pixel for pixel), and the page writes in over 900 ms: the index rolls 14 pt to the new number over 0–0.45, the kicker rises 10 pt over 0–0.4, each headline line rises from its clipped baseline from 3° over 0.06 + 0.1i to that plus 0.5, the caption rises 8 pt over 0.4–0.85 and the link fades in over 0.5–1. The self-playing demo loops every 16 s (LOOP): a virtual finger taps the burger at 1.0 s, lands on Exhibitions at 2.4 s, glides down a word at a time to Journal by 5.3 s and back up to Architecture by 6.2 s, lifts there at 6.8 s (card into the hero of the Architecture page), rests, taps the burger at 10.0 s, glides from Architecture up to Exhibitions between 11.4 and 13.1 s and lifts at 13.6 s, back on the first page, which it rests on until the loop restarts. A touch stops the demo for 4 s, after which an open menu closes, the first page comes back (its hero fades in and its text writes in) and the loop restarts after 1 s of rest. Fast taps reverse the timeline from wherever it is, a tap during a flight lands the card at once, and a lift before the menu is fully open chooses nothing. Under reduced motion the demo does not play, the curtain and words fade instead of moving (no bowed edge, no letter-by-letter rise), the card follows the finger without lag or lean, photos swap without a wipe, a chosen card fades out instead of flying and the hero fades in, and the page text fades in place.

## Reference source

The block is built and running in the Native Cook source repository. Each link below is a file on GitHub. To read one as plain text, replace `https://github.com/Native-Cook/native-cook/blob/` with `https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Native-Cook/native-cook/` in its address.

### Files of the block

- [EditorialMenuMorph.kt](https://github.com/Native-Cook/native-cook/blob/main/kotlin/app/src/main/java/com/ngocdevv/nativecook/blocks/navigation/editorialmenumorph/EditorialMenuMorph.kt)
- [EditorialMenuMorphPages.kt](https://github.com/Native-Cook/native-cook/blob/main/kotlin/app/src/main/java/com/ngocdevv/nativecook/blocks/navigation/editorialmenumorph/EditorialMenuMorphPages.kt)

## Your instructions

_Anything specific to this app goes here: where the block should appear, what to rename, what to change. Left empty, integrate the block as it is._

## How to work

Work like an experienced Android engineer joining an existing project: learn the app first, read only what you need, decide early how the block fits, then integrate it with as little disruption as possible. Take the steps in order.

**Done means** the block is reachable in the user's app and behaves like the reference on an emulator or a device. A Compose preview is useful while you work, but it is not the proof: build, install and run the app.

**Fidelity.** Bring over the real implementation. Keep its structure, colours, sizes, timings and easing. Change only what this project requires and what "Your instructions" ask for.

If you already learned this project earlier in the conversation, reuse what you know and skip step 2. Learn it again only if the project changed or something you need is missing.

### 1. Check where you are

- You need the project's files and a terminal. If this prompt was pasted into a chat that has neither, stop and say so: it has to be run by a coding agent opened on the project.
- Confirm the project is an Android app built with Gradle. If it is something else, stop, say what you found, and do not create a new app inside it unless the instructions ask for one.

### 2. Learn the host app

- The app module, its namespace, `minSdk`, `compileSdk`, and the versions of Kotlin, the Android Gradle Plugin and Compose (a BOM or single versions).
- Whether Compose is switched on in that module, and whether screens are Compose, Views or both.
- Navigation: Navigation Compose, fragments, activities, or a single screen. Find how a screen is added today.
- How dependencies are declared: a version catalog (`libs.versions.toml`) or directly in `build.gradle`.
- Conventions: package layout, naming, theme, where resources live and how they are named.

### 3. Read the block

- Open the demo, then each file in the block's package. The list above names every file of the block, and the resources it uses from outside its package.
- The demo is how the source repository shows the block. Bring over what the demo shows, not the repository's gallery. Anything listed under "Used by the demo only" stays behind.
- Read the block's parameters and their defaults. The demo may switch on an option that makes the block play by itself for a recording (for example `autoPlay`). Keep the option; leave it off in the user's app unless asked.

### 4. Decide the fit

- Compare the block's libraries and the versions it was built with to the host's. Add what is missing the way this project declares dependencies. Do not upgrade the host's Kotlin, Gradle plugin or Compose versions without asking; if an API differs on the host's version, adapt the block's code.
- Check `minSdk`. If the block uses an API newer than the host's minimum, keep the fallback the source has, or tell the user what would be lost.
- If Compose is not switched on in the module, say what turning it on involves before you do it. In a View-based screen, show the block through a `ComposeView`.
- Shared helpers: copy the ones the block imports next to it, or fold them into the block's files. Do not copy helpers it never calls.

### 5. Bring it in

- Copy the block's files into a package of this app, and rewrite the `package` lines and the imports, including the import of the app's own `R` class.
- Copy its resources and asset files. Keep their names unless one collides with a resource of the app; then rename it everywhere it is used.
- Keep reduced-motion handling, haptics and accessibility descriptions as they are in the source. If the block needs a permission, add it to the manifest and say so.
- Mount the block where the instructions say. With no instructions, add a screen or destination named after the block and make it reachable the way the app's other screens are.

### 6. Run it

- Build with the project's own task, for example `./gradlew :app:assembleDebug`, and fix every error and new warning the block introduced.
- Install and run it, and use the block: every state, every gesture, and once with animations switched off in the system settings.
- If the build or the emulator fails for a reason outside the block, report the error and ask how to continue.

### 7. Report

- Files added and changed, dependencies and permissions added, and anything renamed to avoid a collision.
- How to reach the block in the app.
- Anything that differs from the reference, and why.
